headline: 3 named Ethereum contracts discovered from Etherscan name-tag search; multi-chain addresses not yet enumerated per chain; no canonical deployments doc or GitHub artifact found.

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search for 'Team Finance' / 'TrustSwap' surfaced three labelled addresses on Ethereum: 0xE2fE530C047f2d85298b07D9333C05737f1435fB ('TrustSwap: Team Finance Lock'), 0x64D06dcc12fA07e302f052a9F5BC1aa11e29D9E2 ('TrustSwap: Team Finance Vesting'), and 0x0c89c0407775dd89b12918b9c0aa42bf96518820 ('TrustSwap: Team Finance Security' — seen active on BSC). blockscan.com confirms the Lock contract is active across Ethereum and BSC. Per-chain explorer sweeps for Avalanche, Polygon, Base, Arbitrum, Blast, Cronos, Fantom, Kava, Flare, Klaytn, Odyssey, Mantle, LUKSO, Berachain, and Pulse were not completed due to tool-call budget exhaustion.

The handbook/docs site (handbook.team.finance) was fetched. No canonical 'Deployed Contracts' or 'Addresses' page was found; the docs cover product features and auditor partnerships but do not list deployed contract addresses. protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc is set to null.

protocol.audit_links points to https://www.team.finance/file/audit.pdf; the fetch redirected to the Team Finance Security handbook page (handbook.team.finance/team-finance-security-and-audits), which references audits by Hacken and Chainsulting (for contracts) and a BailSec audit for the SWAP token, but provides no address-table PDF with in-scope contract addresses. The PDF itself was not retrievable as binary. The security/audits page on the main site names CertiK, Hacken, and BailSec as auditors. No audit-era addresses were extracted.

The protocol.github slug is 'team-finance' (not a full URL). A search query for 'site:github.com team-finance contracts deployments addresses' did not return the Team Finance GitHub organisation or any deployment artifact files. GitHub artifacts (broadcast JSONs, hardhat-deploy files, addresses.json) could not be fetched within remaining tool budget. No SHA-pinned deployment file was found.

Protocol spans 17 chains (Ethereum, Binance, Base, Avalanche, Polygon, Pulse, Arbitrum, Blast, Cronos, Fantom, Kava, Flare, Klaytn, Odyssey, Mantle, LUKSO, Berachain). Only Ethereum addresses were surfaced from block-explorer name-tag searches. BSC activity for 0x0c89c0407775dd89b12918b9c0aa42bf96518820 ('TrustSwap: Team Finance Security') was observed on blockscan.com but not verified via bscscan.com directly. Addresses for Base, Avalanche, Polygon, Pulse, Arbitrum, Blast, Cronos, Fantom, Kava, Flare, Klaytn, Odyssey, Mantle, LUKSO, and Berachain remain undiscovered.

The Vesting contract 0x64D06dcc12fA07e302f052a9F5BC1aa11e29D9E2 is labelled 'VestingFactory' on Etherscan. Factory child enumeration via the DeFiPunkd read API was not performed due to tool-call budget exhaustion. The Lock contract at 0xE2fE530C047f2d85298b07D9333C05737f1435fB is a proxy; its implementation address is referenced as similar to 0x7bAf06a9...9746C77f5 (truncated, full address not confirmed).

Role taxonomy applied: Lock contract = 'vault' (token locker), Vesting contract = 'factory' (VestingFactory), Security contract = 'other' (role unclear from available data). All actor_classes set to 'unknown' pending ABI reads.

All three admin_addresses[] entries trace to etherscan.io / blockscan.com search results fetched in this run. The truncated implementation address 0x7bAf06a9...9746C77f5 is a snippet-only sighting and is placed in unknowns[], not admin_addresses[].

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked the protocol website, docs/handbook, security page, and performed Etherscan/blockscan name-tag searches, surfacing 3 named contracts on Ethereum. Multi-chain enumeration across 16 additional chains and GitHub deployment artifacts remain incomplete. Grade is unknown pending fuller on-chain evidence.

evidence.shows: Protocol website confirms Team Finance is a token-management platform (lock, vest, stake, airdrop, payroll, multisend) operating on 30+ chains, owned by TrustSwap Inc., audited by CertiK, Hacken, and BailSec.
Security page names CertiK, Hacken, and BailSec as auditors; no deployed contract addresses listed.

Audit PDF URL redirects to handbook security page (handbook.team.finance/team-finance-security-and-audits) which references Hacken and Chainsulting for contract audits and BailSec for SWAP token; no contract address table found.

Docs index page: confirms Team Finance is non-custodial, describes services (locks, vesting, staking, airdrop, payroll, multisend, token generation), founded 2020, part of TrustSwap ecosystem. No deployed contract addresses listed.

Address 0xE2fE530C047f2d85298b07D9333C05737f1435fB labelled 'TrustSwap: Team Finance Lock' on Etherscan; proxy contract with implementation similar to 0x7bAf06a9...9746C77f5; source includes LockToken.sol with OpenZeppelin Ownable and Pausable.
Address 0x64D06dcc12fA07e302f052a9F5BC1aa11e29D9E2 labelled 'TrustSwap: Team Finance Vesting' and described as 'VestingFactory' on Etherscan; creator 0x43affF62...D44eEe68D.

Address 0x0c89c0407775dd89b12918b9c0aa42bf96518820 labelled 'TrustSwap: Team Finance Security' on blockscan.com; shown as active on BSC (withdraw tokens, fee flows); also listed as active on Ethereum.
Lock contract 0xE2fE530C047f2d85298b07D9333C05737f1435fB shown active with recent Withdraw Tokens and Transfer Locks transactions on Ethereum through October 2026.

protocol_metadata.about: Team Finance is a non-custodial token-management platform for Web3 projects, enabling users to lock team tokens and LP tokens in time-released smart contract vaults, create vesting schedules for investors and employees, and launch staking pools and airdrops. It supports 30+ blockchains and is used by 40,000+ projects. The platform is a product of TrustSwap Inc. and operates across EVM and non-EVM chains without admin keys or custodial access to locked assets.
